title: When Things Fall Apart
coreMove: Convert private pressure into clear facts, clean people calls, and controlled execution.
sourcePressure: Collapse requires direct communication, layoffs or role-fit corrections when needed, dignity, speed without panic, and refusal to plan around rescue fantasies.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is blunt toughness: say hard things, make cuts, and push through.

exampleSpecs.domain: regional ambulance service after a contract loss
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations chief deciding whether to close two stations or quietly hope for replacement funding
exampleSpecs.stakes: crews, response times, town councils, and patient coverage all face real harm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chief posts the lost-contract number, names the two stations affected, and schedules individual crew meetings before the dispatch rumor channel fills the gap
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dispatch map with two station pins covered by orange tape

exampleSpecs.domain: medical device startup recalling a faulty sensor batch
exampleSpecs.audience: a CEO whose head of quality keeps minimizing the defect
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients, regulators, and the company's survival depend on fast factual action
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the CEO asks the quality head to state the defect rate in front of legal and operations, then removes ambiguity about recall ownership before the next shipment leaves
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tray of returned sensors with red quarantine labels

exampleSpecs.domain: regional newspaper after advertising revenue collapses
exampleSpecs.audience: a publisher deciding between serial cuts and one clear restructuring
exampleSpecs.stakes: serial uncertainty could bleed reporters and reduce local coverage further
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the publisher compares the three-round cut plan with one decisive plan, then chooses the cleaner reduction and writes the exact coverage promise that remains
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a newsroom assignment board with blank spaces where ads used to be pinned

exampleSpecs.domain: specialty chemicals plant after an executive safety misfit
exampleSpecs.audience: a plant president whose operations VP keeps bypassing shutdown procedures
exampleSpecs.stakes: normalizing the misfit risks injury and teaches supervisors the wrong standard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the president holds up the bypass log, states the role expectation, and removes the VP from shutdown authority before the next production run
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bypass log with three supervisor initials in the margin

exampleSpecs.domain: independent childcare network after an insurer cancellation
exampleSpecs.audience: an executive director tempted to keep accepting enrollments while seeking a last-minute quote
exampleSpecs.stakes: parents need truth, staff need jobs, and operating uninsured is not an option
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director stops enrollment, names the insurance gap to site leads, and assigns parent calls instead of building a plan around a quote that has not arrived
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an insurance cancellation notice folded under a stack of enrollment forms

exampleSpecs.domain: data-center operator after a major customer churns
exampleSpecs.audience: a general manager choosing between hiding the churn and renegotiating vendor commitments
exampleSpecs.stakes: if staff hear it sideways, they will slow work and vendors will learn first
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager converts the churn email into a factual internal note, makes the vendor-call list, and refuses to call a speculative replacement deal the plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a customer termination email open beside a rack-power invoice

skillTargets: choose candor that creates shared reality
separate dignity from delay in layoffs
identify executive misfit as an organizational cost
reject plans that depend on unconfirmed rescue

tryThisNowSpec: Find one fact people are likely to learn through rumor. Write the exact plain sentence that states it, the affected group, and the next decision boundary.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
